title: Dynamic tenant-aware batching profiles and rollbackable quant mapper
author: Priya Rao
ci_status: pass (with one rerun for flaky e2e)
description:
Motivation: customers with mixed-tenancy workloads were seeing inconsistent unit economics because a single global batching/cache default treats all tenants the same. This PR introduces tenant-aware batching profiles that are computed from recent per-tenant latency and cost telemetry and a rollbackable quantization mapper that lets control-plane operators stage quant profiles and automatically fall back to a conservative safe profile on quality regressions. Changes are conservative and behind a feature flag by default.

Summary of changes: compute tenant-specific batching presets on the control plane; expose a policy API to pin or override tenant presets; runtime picks tenant profile via connection metadata and applies batching windows and kv-cache timeouts; quant mapper is separate service that stores candidate quant profiles as immutable revisions and provides a runtime-safe pointer that can be switched atomically; health checks monitor token-level loss/likelihood deltas and trigger automatic rollback.

Checklist: 
- [x] Control plane PR: tenant profile generator service + scheduler
- [x] Runtime PR: profile fetch + batching adapter + metric hooks
- [x] Quant mapper service: revisioned profiles + safe fallback wiring
- [x] Telemetry: per-tenant unit-econ metrics, rollback events, SLA breach counters
- [x] End-to-end integration tests (canary)
- [x] Rollout plan and docs

Testing and verification: unit tests for generator heuristics and mapper safety, integration tests with local runtime that simulate tenant churn and quant regressions, a canary deployment limited to a single region and three low-traffic tenants. CI initially failed on an unrelated flaky e2e (session-restore) — rerun passed. Load tests show a 9-14% reduction in per-token cost for targeted tenants with no measurable average latency regression under the canary.

Risk and mitigations: quant changes are the highest risk. We implemented immutable revisions and an automatic rollback monitor based on evaluation hooks (per-tenant perplexity delta and top-k distribution drift). The feature flag is off by default; rollout is staged (opt-in tenants -> canary -> gradual percentage rollout) and includes an emergency kill switch in the console.

Rollout plan: merge gated behind product feature flag. Initial canary in us-west-2 for three opt-in tenants for 48 hours, then 10% gradual rollout over 2 days, followed by global expand if metrics are stable for 24h.

Notes: includes a short-lived migration that creates tenant_profile metadata rows; migration is reversible and idempotent. Documentation added to ops/runbooks/tenant-batch-and-quant.md.

review_comments:
Elias Park: Overall looks good. Two concerns: 1) the recompute frequency default (15m) might be noisy for low-traffic tenants; suggest adding a min-sample threshold. 2) add a metric to count automatic rollbacks per-tenant so we can detect misbehaving tenants.
Author (Priya): added min-sample threshold and rollback counter in next commit.

Monica Li: For the quant mapper, make sure we have a manual pin API and an audit log for profile switches. Also request an integration test that simulates a marginal quality regression and automatic rollback.
Author: added pin/override endpoints and audit events; added integration scenario. Monica: approving after one nit on error messages.

Samir Gupta: Can we avoid a hot path RPC in runtime on every request? Suggest caching the profile pointer in the connection state and a background refresh.
Author: implemented connection-level caching with TTL and fallback to global default; updated tests. Samir: approved.
CI Bot: e2e/session-restore failed on first run; rerun completed successfully.
merge_outcome: merged via squash on 2025-02-01 after approvals from Monica Li and Samir Gupta; noted canary gating and feature flag off by default
release_notes: Introduce tenant-aware batching profiles and rollbackable quant mapper: tenant-level presets reduce per-token cost for targeted tenants, quant changes are staged and automatically rolled back on quality regressions. Feature flagged and rolled out as a canary. See ops/runbooks/tenant-batch-and-quant.md for rollout steps.
additional_notes: Performance: canary saw 9-14% per-token cost improvements for opt-in tenants with no SLA regressions.
Telemetry: new metrics prefixed with tenant_profile.* and quant_mapper.rollback.*
Ops: emergency kill switch exposed in console and cli (redwoodctl disable-tenant-profiles)
Follow-ups: 1) investigate multi-tenant profile blending for shared GPU pools (ENG-2122), 2) add tenant-level simulation UI in console
